title: Manitoba man dies after RCMP use pepper spray
subtitle: 3 other deaths in Canada since 2001
article: An altercation with police that left a Manitoba man dead on the weekend appears to be the fourth pepper-spray related death since 2001 in Canada.
Nathan Boryskavich, 43, of Belmont, died Saturday after being hit with pepper spray by RCMP in The Pas, Man.

Boryskavich had been removed from his ex-wife's home in The Pas, about 600 kilometres northwest of Winnipeg. Officers managed to arrest him, but police say he became combative. RCMP spokesman Sgt. Line Karpish said there was a struggle, and police used pepper spray against him.
Karpish said officers then noticed Boryskavich was in medical distress and took him to the hospital, where he died on Saturday. An autopsy was to be conducted Monday in Winnipeg.
Boryskavich apparently suffered from asthma, CBC News has learned.
Three other known cases of people succumbing following the use of pepper spray occurred in Regina, most recently in October of this year.
In all four situations, pepper spray was used to subdue a suspect during a struggle with the police.
The RCMP refer to pepper spray as "OC spray," which stands for oleoresin capsicum.
It is a derivative of pepper plants and is similar to domestically available bear spray - a consumer product the Manitoba government plans to restrict this year.
Exposure to pepper spray causes intense burning of the eyes, shortness of breath and coughing.
Manitoba's chief medical examiner will begin an autopsy on the deceased man from The Pas Monday.
If it is determined that the cause of death is anything but from natural reasons, an inquest will be held to review the circumstances.
